sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Massachusetts, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 27Passed

Your application must be received by your city or town clerk before 5 p.m. on the fifth business day before the election: Tuesday, October 27, 2026. Because mail can take up to a week each way, Boston advises applying two to three weeks ahead. (the law)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must reach your city or town clerk, or a drop box, by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, when polls close. A ballot mailed on or before Election Day still counts if it arrives by 5 p.m. on Friday, November 6, 2026 (the third day after the election). A readable postmark shows when it was mailed. (the law)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Friday, October 30, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Massachusetts’s own site

At school away from home, in Massachusetts or in another state? What Massachusetts says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No. Every registered voter may vote early by mail for the state election; no reason is needed. The state mails every registered voter an application before the first state election of the year, but you must send it back (or apply another way) to get a ballot. (the law)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Apply through the state's Mail-in Ballot Application System. You can have the ballot sent to your home or another mailing address; no handwritten signature is needed. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Sign the application the state mailed you (or one printed from your city or town's website, or any signed letter asking for a mail ballot with your name, address and where to mail the ballot) and send it to your city or town clerk. An electronic signature must look like your handwritten one; a typed name is not accepted. (official page)
  • E-mail, fax or in person. Many city and town clerks also take a scanned signed application by e-mail or fax, or in person at the clerk's office. Do not put the application in a ballot drop box. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the envelope provided (postage is covered). Mailed by Election Day and received by 5 p.m. on Friday, November 6. (the law)
  • Drop box. A secured drop box for the city or town where you are registered, by 8 p.m. on Election Day. (the law)
  • In person. At your city or town clerk's office by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or at an early voting location in your city or town during early voting hours. You or a family member may return it. (the law)

What the envelope needs

Fill out and sign the statement printed on the inner envelope. The clerk compares that signature with the one on your application. No witness is needed. Some first-time voters must also send a copy of an ID that shows their name and address; if you must, the clerk sends a notice with your ballot, and the copy goes on the outside of the ballot envelope. If something is wrong with the envelope, the clerk marks it rejected, tells you, and sends a new ballot. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Massachusetts’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Saturday, October 17, 2026 to Friday, October 30, 2026.

Early voting in person for the state election runs from Saturday, October 17 through Friday, October 30, 2026 (dates posted by the Boston Election Department; each city or town sets its own hours and places). (official page)

Students

At school in Massachusetts, away from home

Students going to school in Massachusetts may consider either their school address or their home address as their residence for voting, and register at that one address. A student who stays registered at home in another Massachusetts city or town can apply for a mail ballot from that home city or town and have it sent to the school address. You may not be registered in more than one place. (official page)

At school in another state, with Massachusetts as home

A Massachusetts resident going to school in another state who still considers the Massachusetts home their voting residence can ask their city or town to mail them a ballot, and should allow enough time for it to reach them and come back. A student from another state going to school in Massachusetts may stay registered at home and vote absentee from there, or register at the Massachusetts address, but not both. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military members, their families and U.S. citizens living overseas can register and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application and use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup. The request (by mail, e-mail or fax) must be received by 5 p.m. on Tuesday, October 27, 2026. A ballot returned by e-mail, online or fax must be received by 8 p.m. on November 3. A ballot mailed by November 3 must arrive by 5 p.m. on the third day after the election if mailed inside the U.S., or by 5 p.m. on the tenth day after (Friday, November 13, 2026) if mailed from outside the U.S. (federal guide)

Massachusetts in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The Massachusetts registration deadline for this election is Saturday, October 24, 2026 (Boston's page).
  • Worcester's student page still says an absentee ballot can be requested until noon the day before the election; under current state law that noon deadline is for absentee ballots voted in person at the clerk's office. A ballot to be mailed must be applied for by 5 p.m. on October 27.
  • If the tracker shows your mailed ballot has not arrived, Boston says you may vote in person on Election Day; the mailed ballot is then set aside when it arrives.
  • State law also lists attending a college or university away from your city or town as a reason for an absentee ballot (General Laws, Chapter 54, Section 86); for the state election anyone may vote early by mail without a reason.

How this was checked

  • The Secretary of the Commonwealth's website (sec.state.ma.us) answered this check with a check for human visitors, so its pages were not read. Facts come from the state's General Laws and from the Boston and Worcester election offices. The online application and the ballot tracker are the state's own tools, linked from Boston's page; they were not opened here.
Where this comes from: 6 pages of Massachusetts’s election office, its laws and the federal guide

  2. Vote by Mail in Boston, City of Boston Election Department (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  3. Students, City of Worcester Election Commission (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  4. General Laws, Chapter 54, Section 86 (who may vote absentee, including college attendance), General Court of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (the law; read October 21, 2026)
  5. Massachusetts 2026-2027 Voting Assistance Guide, Federal Voting Assistance Program (U.S. Department of Defense) (federal guide; read October 21, 2026)
  6. General Laws, Chapter 54, Section 89 (applications for absent voting ballots), General Court of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (the law; read October 21, 2026)

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: Massachusetts’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.
